about.title: Hayward Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products rarely announce themselves. A space heater bought off Mission Boulevard, a child seat that gave way in a collision on I-880, a power tool in a Hayward garage — the flaw usually surfaces only after someone is hurt. California treats these cases differently from most injury claims. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. What matters is whether the product carried a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and whether that defect caused your injury. Hayward sits at a busy junction in Alameda County, and I-880 in both directions appears often in the public record of the 474 injury collisions logged here in 2025. When a crash involves a failed brake, airbag, or tire, the claim may reach beyond the other driver to the company that built the part. If a product hurt you or a family member, keep the item, its packaging, and any receipts. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects Hayward residents with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

items.title: Strict Liability Knowledge
items.desc: Attorneys in our network understand that California product cases usually turn on the defect and the harm it caused, not on proving the manufacturer acted negligently. That framing shapes how evidence is gathered from day one.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Hayward retailer that sold the item may each bear responsibility under California law. An independent attorney can identify all of them rather than stopping at the first name on the box.

items.title: Preserving the Product
items.desc: The item itself is the heart of a defect claim, whether it is a cracked helmet or a failed airbag module. The attorney you are matched with can advise on keeping it intact and, when needed, arranging an expert inspection.

items.question: My car's airbag didn't deploy in a crash on I-880 in Hayward. Is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be. Even when another driver caused the collision, a component that failed to perform as designed may give rise to a separate strict liability claim against the manufacturer or supplier. Do not let the vehicle be scrapped or repaired before an attorney has a chance to preserve it. An independent lawyer can evaluate whether the failure points to a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the maker was careful or careless is usually not the central question. Your attorney will still need evidence, so keeping the product and documenting your injuries matters a great deal.
